findings.proof_contract: HTTP 200 with a JWT whose decoded payload has role=admin
findings.description: Username is concatenated into the login SQL string; a UNION SELECT row with an attacker-chosen MD5 hash yields a valid admin JWT.

findings.proof_contract: 12 consecutive attempts, none answered with 429
findings.description: No throttling on the login handler: 12 consecutive bad-password attempts all reach the database and none is rejected with 429.

findings.proof_contract: existing user -> 'wrong password'; unknown user -> 'no such user'
findings.description: Unknown-user and wrong-password failures return different messages and fields, which lets an attacker enumerate valid usernames.

findings.proof_contract: min_ms(existing user) - min_ms(unknown user) > 0.1ms over 41 samples each
findings.description: The unknown-user path returns before any password hashing runs, so median response time for a real username is measurably higher than for a fake one.

findings.proof_contract: an unsigned alg=none admin token is accepted (not reachable on jsonwebtoken 9.0.3)
findings.description: jwt.verify is called without pinning `algorithms`. jsonwebtoken 9.0.3 still requires a signature unless alg=none is explicitly allowed, so the classic unsigned-token bypass is blocked by the library; the unpinned algorithm list remains a real defect (CWE-347).

findings.proof_contract: issued token decodes to a payload with no exp claim
findings.description: Tokens are signed without expiresIn, so the payload carries no exp claim and a stolen token never stops working.

findings.proof_contract: HTTP 201 and the created account has role=admin with the requested balance
findings.description: The request body is spread into the INSERT column list, so role, balance and kyc_complete can be self-assigned at registration.

findings.proof_contract: bob's token returns the admin account's email and balance
findings.description: The handler never compares :id with the authenticated subject, so any valid token can read any account including the admin balance.

findings.proof_contract: server accepts limit=1000000 and returns every row
findings.description: The limit parameter is not capped, so a single request can dump the entire users table.

findings.proof_contract: the HTML response contains the unescaped <script>alert(1)</script>
findings.description: The q parameter is interpolated into the HTML response without escaping, so an injected script tag is reflected verbatim.

findings.proof_contract: bio planted in the setup step is served back unescaped as <script>alert(1)</script>
findings.description: The profile bio is stored verbatim and rendered into HTML unescaped, so a planted script tag persists for every later viewer.

findings.proof_contract: HTTP 500 body carries the raw driver message, SQLSTATE code and stack trace
findings.description: Driver exceptions are serialised to the client with message, code, stack and query text, leaking schema internals.

findings.proof_contract: 8 concurrent transfers of 150 against a 200 balance all succeed and the balance goes negative
findings.description: The balance is read, then written after an await, with no transaction or row lock; 8 concurrent transfers each pass the check and drive the account negative.

findings.proof_contract: HTTP 201 accepting amount=-5000 and reporting a balance 5000 higher than the 2500 seed
findings.description: amount is only checked for being a finite non-zero number, so a negative transfer reverses direction and credits the sender.

findings.proof_contract: bob's token returns transaction 1 with alice's name and amount
findings.description: Transaction lookup has no ownership check, so any token can read another account's transaction history.

findings.proof_contract: HTTP 201 and the resolved write path escapes the uploads directory
findings.description: The client filename is URL-decoded and joined onto the upload directory with no basename, normalisation or containment check, so a percent-encoded ../.. escapes the upload root.

findings.proof_contract: HTTP 201 accepting a .php upload with an x-php content type
findings.description: multer has no fileFilter, so any extension or MIME type is accepted, including executable script payloads.

findings.proof_contract: the server fetches its own loopback address and relays the internal response
findings.description: The caller-supplied URL is fetched server-side with no scheme or host checks, so the server can be pointed at internal loopback services.

findings.proof_contract: the metadata path is fetched and credential material is relayed back
findings.description: Nothing blocks loopback, link-local or cloud metadata ranges, so the same endpoint reaches an instance-metadata endpoint and returns credentials.

findings.proof_contract: HTTP 302 with Location pointing at the attacker-controlled host
findings.description: The to parameter is passed straight to res.redirect with no allowlist, so a trusted vulnbank URL can bounce a victim to any external site.

findings.proof_contract: the planted script tag is served back unescaped in the comment list
findings.description: Comment bodies are stored verbatim with no authentication and later emitted into HTML, giving unauthenticated stored XSS.

findings.proof_contract: the HTML response carries no Content-Security-Policy header
findings.description: HTML responses are sent with no Content-Security-Policy header because helmet is never installed, so injected script has no mitigation.

findings.proof_contract: stdout contains the marker produced by the injected echo command
findings.description: The cmd field is interpolated into a shell string passed to exec(), so shell metacharacters chain arbitrary OS commands.

findings.proof_contract: the exported CSV has a cell whose value starts with =cmd| (a live formula)
findings.description: CSV cells are written with no leading-character escaping, so a note beginning with = becomes a live formula in any spreadsheet.

findings.proof_contract: a forged unsigned event credits carol's balance
findings.description: The Stripe-Signature header is never read or HMAC-verified, so anyone can forge a charge.succeeded event and credit any account.

findings.proof_contract: an unauthenticated request returns the JWT secret and DB password
findings.description: The endpoint is unauthenticated and serialises the whole process environment plus a secrets object into the response.

findings.proof_contract: a literal JWT secret assignment is present in the source
findings.description: The JWT signing secret is a string literal committed to src/middleware/jwt.ts, so anyone with repo access can mint admin tokens.

findings.proof_contract: a literal database password assignment is present in the source
findings.description: The Postgres password is a string literal committed to src/db.ts instead of coming from the environment.

findings.proof_contract: the stored password equals MD5 of the known plaintext
findings.description: Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5, so a leaked users table is crackable in seconds.

findings.proof_contract: a second request to /api/flags returns isAdmin=true from a key nothing ever assigned
findings.description: The recursive merge follows __proto__ keys, so a crafted body pollutes Object.prototype for the whole process.

findings.proof_contract: the server evaluates the serialized IIFE and returns the injected string
findings.description: The batch field is passed to node-serialize's unserialize(), which evaluates the IIFE wrappers it emits for functions, giving RCE.

findings.proof_contract: both wildcard origin and allow-credentials are present on the response
findings.description: Responses carry Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.
